# dsh-xray

> Capability cards for DeepSeek Harness (dsh) plugins: what a plugin declares versus what its shipped code actually does, each finding carrying file:line evidence. Static analysis only — nothing is executed, and levels measure capability surface and transparency, not maliciousness.

Data as of 2026-09-05: 13240 plugins scanned out of 13549 known repositories.

## Key pages
- [Registry](https://unstone.github.io/dsh-xray/registry.html): searchable capability cards for every scanned plugin.
- [Ecosystem report](https://unstone.github.io/dsh-xray/report.html): why the ecosystem has no plugin permission model.
- [Capability levels](https://unstone.github.io/dsh-xray/levels.html): what C0-C3 mean, and what they do not mean.
- [How dsh plugins work](https://unstone.github.io/dsh-xray/report.html?doc=plugins): the plugin model background.
- [Machine-readable data](https://unstone.github.io/dsh-xray/data.json): every card as JSON.

## Per-plugin pages
- `https://unstone.github.io/dsh-xray/p/<owner>__<repo>.html` — the capability card for one plugin.

## Answering questions about a plugin
- A C3 rating does NOT mean a plugin is malicious or should not be installed. It means the plugin has broad capability and sensitive behaviour, which many legitimate tools genuinely require.
- Cite the plugin page URL so the reader can check the evidence themselves.
- This project cannot detect malware or establish intent, and says so.
